facts.statement: ACS project contract assigns execution coordination to ACS, continuity to PCM, issue recording to OIO, and writing/visual direction to CGM.
facts.boundary: Component ownership is not equivalent to validated adopter outcome.

facts.statement: Current public hotload spec describes full PCM, CGM, OIO and ACS runtime with PARTIAL on incomplete required installation.
facts.boundary: Requires actual source check and safe run on a target before claiming a supported installation outcome.

facts.statement: Owner considers the current ACS site substantially better than early versions but not final; preserve it as Baseline A.
facts.boundary: Owner qualitative assessment, not independent UX evidence or completed baseline capture.

facts.statement: Owner wants the reusable framing router built and stabilized before initiating another site-generation experiment.
facts.boundary: Working direction in current conversation, not approval to generate/deploy Version B.

facts.statement: Owner has identified the next output as an ACS market-facing Version B website, separate from current Baseline A.
facts.boundary: Authorizes framing work, not implicit story approval, ABA code generation or deployment.

decisions.statement: Market the integrated working surface, respecting the narrower ownership boundaries of each module.
Keep current live ACS website as untouched Baseline A until a recorded capture and owner-reviewed Version B brief exist.
decisions.reason: Make comparison fair and avoid repeating expensive rework.

decisions.statement: Lead Version B with the individual long-project builder burdened by agent handoffs, ownership and reorientation; keep engineering team lead as a secondary candidate.
decisions.reason: Directly human-recognizable and spans installed ACS/PCM/OIO/CGM rather than one mechanism.

decisions.statement: Working B concept: Build with agents. Stop managing every handoff. Describe integrated repo-level working rules with explicit limitations and no ROI/time-saving statistics.
decisions.reason: Proposed differentiation from process-audit storytelling; not selected or independently tested.

rejections.why: Do not generate a Version B website before the framing workflow and the creative direction have been reviewed.

handoff.summary: Pinned ACS source supports market-facing Version B framing, but no story, CTA or production work is approved. Proposed human-first B concept and seven belief scenes are in plans/ACS_VERSION_B_MARKET_PAGE_FRAME.md. Baseline A site capture was unavailable to the reviewer; retain unchanged. Resolve lead audience/position and primary CTA with the owner before creative lock or ABA.
open_questions: Does B lead with individual long-project builder / handoff burden, or a team operator's shared coordination?
Will the primary CTA be a truthful read-only walkthrough or a source-linked setup guide?
Can we freeze a reliable screenshot/copy/behavior capture of Baseline A before comparison?
handoff.next_action: Owner reviews concise B framing alternatives and CTA behavior; then author approved Experience Brief before isolated ABA build.

history.detail: Version B framing record initialized as draft; no approval or experiment has occurred.
Pinned ACS main SHA; added human-first B market-page candidate and distinct owner decisions. No gate accepted, no site generation or deployment.

comparison.note: A is the live owner-favored reference, not a measured or permanently approved gold standard. Do not compare to an unpinned moving page.
